    title: People eat well
    level: impact
    addressesEffects: [eff-diabetes]

With element commands:

impact-model cause add impact-model.yaml --id cause-fast-food \
  --statement "Fast food is everywhere" --level underlying --parents cause-busy
impact-model effect add impact-model.yaml --id eff-costs \
  --statement "Higher health costs" --parents eff-diabetes
impact-model outcome set impact-model.yaml oc-eat-well --relieves eff-diabetes

docs.title: Causes and effects form a network
docs.text: A cause can contribute to several others, and an effect can follow from several others, so parents is a list. A tree is the case of at most one parent each. Validation rejects a cause or effect that is its own parent, and a chain of parents that leads back to where it started through any branch.

docs.title: Which way the links point
docs.text: A cause's parents point from the deeper cause toward the problem: structural causes feed underlying ones, underlying causes feed immediate ones, and immediate causes lead to the core problem. Written the other way round, the tree draws upside down, so IMP-CAU-003 reports a cause whose parent sits at a deeper level.

docs.title: How the diagram is laid out
docs.text:
The arrows flow upward, from the roots to the core problem and on to the branches:

  • The core problem is in the middle row.
  • A cause with no parents is in the first row below it. Any other cause is one row below its lowest parent, so every arrow from a cause points up.
  • An effect with no parents is in the first row above the core problem. Any other effect is one row above its highest parent.
  • Within a row, boxes keep the order of the model file.
  • A cause or effect set aside is drawn faded and labelled "(set aside)". A rejected one is left out.

The diagram is built first as a JSON document, a d2vision diagram spec with a zone for the effects, the core problem, and the causes, a row for each layer, and the edges between boxes. problem-tree-json prints that document, and D2 and Mermaid are both rendered from it, so another tool can read or restyle the same tree. D2 keeps every row in place; Mermaid draws bottom to top and places the rows itself.

docs.title: The tables
docs.text:
Below the diagram, problem-tree and problem-tree-d2 list:

  • each cause with its level, what it leads to, and the outcomes that address it
  • each effect with what it follows from and the outcomes that relieve it

A dash means nothing addresses it yet, and "set aside" gives the reason.

docs.title: What lint checks
docs.text: Rule Checks IMP-CAU-001 Each underlying and structural cause is addressed by an outcome or set aside IMP-CAU-002 Outcomes address some root cause, not only immediate ones IMP-CAU-003 A cause contributes only to causes at its own level or nearer the problem IMP-EFF-001 Each effect is relieved by an outcome or set aside IMP-EFF-002 Effects are relieved by long-term or impact outcomes, not only earlier ones

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Labels are not wrapped, so a long problem statement makes a wide box. Keep the core problem to a short phrase and put the detail in the context's narrative.
  • Within a row, boxes keep file order, so arrows can cross. Reordering causes or effects in the file reorders the row.

docs.title: Quality and Judging
docs.text:
Three layers check an impact model, from cheapest to most thorough. Each one assumes the one before it passes.

Layer Question Command Needs a model? Validate Is the document well formed? validate No Lint Is the impact model sound? lint No Judge Does an expert reader think it is good? judge A judge, human or agent

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
impact-model validate impact-model.yaml

Checks the schema and the structure: duplicate IDs, references that do not resolve, invalid values, bad dates, group logic, and that nested groups share a target. It also checks observation sets (--model), a child against its parent (--parent), and competing futures (--registry --futures). Exit code 1 means at least one file has errors.

docs.title: Lint
docs.text:
impact-model lint impact-model.yaml --profile standard
impact-model lint --list

Validation says a document is well formed; lint says whether the impact model is sound. There are 72 deterministic rules, each with an ID such as IMP-LOG-001, grouped by what they look at:

Area What the rules look for Structure (STR) At least one impact outcome; no cycles unless marked as feedback; every outcome leads to impact and has a precondition or an intervention; links run from lower levels to higher ones; precondition groups are complete Logic (LOG) Links into medium-term and higher outcomes say why they hold and name an assumption; impact outcomes have at least two preconditions; several incoming links say whether all, any, or some are needed Assumptions and risks (ASM, RSK) High and critical assumptions say how they will be tested, cite evidence, and have a related risk with a mitigation Measurement (MEA, MET, CLM) Every outcome within the ceiling is measured; every indicator has a baseline, target, source, and frequency; targets fall inside the time horizon; claims above the ceiling are contribution, not attribution; common metrics are measured in every pathway Collection budget (BUD) Selected indicators fit the staff-time and question budgets and say how data is collected Accountability and responsibility (ACC, RSP, ACT, INT) A ceiling is declared; outcomes above it are not owned; shared and partner outcomes name who delivers them; every intervention has an owner The chain from activity to impact (INT) Every intervention says what it produces, leads through the outcomes it targets to an impact, agrees with the links that name it, is measured, and states its resources North Stars and headline lists (NSM, HLN, AUD, CTX) A North Star measures an outcome at or below the ceiling, has a baseline, a target, and a guardrail, and belongs to its own pathway; a headline list is short, reported to its audience, and producible; an audience told about outcomes is also told numbers; the impact model states its mission or vision Provenance and evidence (PRV, EVD) Every element says where it comes from; stated elements cite a source; an approved impact model has no hypotheses among what the organization answers for Equity, causes, audiences (EQU, CAU, AUD) Outcomes for target groups are measured by those groups; each deeper cause is addressed or set aside with a reason, and no cause contributes to a deeper one; every audience is the target of something reported Effects (EFF) Each effect in the problem tree is relieved by an outcome or set aside with a reason, and effects are relieved by long-term or impact outcomes, not only earlier ones Pathways and validation (PTH, VAL) Every pathway reaches impact and has a selected indicator; the main steps have been checked with the people the impact model concerns DMAIC readiness (DMA) For a pathway marked projections: [dmaic]: every indicator says how often it is measured and where the data comes from, is measured at least 20 times a year, and, for a survey, gets at least 30 responses per measurement. Pathways not marked are not checked

Profiles choose how much is reported:

Profile Reports draft Errors and structural rules. A small valid impact model is GO standard Also the warnings (the default) full Also the advice

The result is GO unless a rule reports an error (exit code 1). --disable skips rules by ID, and --format json prints a structured-evaluation summary report. Rejected elements are ignored.

docs.title: Judge
docs.text:
A rubric is better than a checklist when the question needs judgment: is the causal logic plausible, is the problem framed fairly, would the people it concerns recognise themselves. The judge commands prepare an impact model for a judge and combine the verdicts. They make no model calls: a human reviewer or an AI agent reads the bundle and returns a verdict.

impact-model judge show impact-model.yaml --profile development --out bundle.json
impact-model judge record impact-model.yaml verdict.json --judge reviewer-a
impact-model judge record impact-model.yaml verdict2.json --judge reviewer-b
impact-model judge summary impact-model.yaml --aggregation majority
  1. show prints the bundle: the rubric, the document, a narrative, the lint report, instructions, and a hash of all of them. Restricted evidence is redacted.
  2. The judge returns a verdict, a structured-evaluation report that scores each rubric category and names its findings.
  3. record checks the verdict against the bundle and stores it under .toc/judgements/<hash>/<judge>.json. It is rejected, with exit code 1, if it judged a different version of the impact model, is not a valid report, scores a category the rubric does not have, or leaves a required category unscored.
  4. summary combines every verdict for the current version: per-category scores, how closely the judges agree, and whether the impact model passes.

Rubric profiles: core has 12 categories; development adds categories for programs working on development outcomes. Aggregation is majority (a tie goes to partial), conservative (the lowest score), optimistic (the highest), or unanimous (anything else is partial). The impact model passes when every required category passes, no blocking category fails, and the findings stay within the rubric's limits.

How well does the rubric discriminate?

The rubric evaluation records two judges scoring a reference impact model and a deliberately weak one. The weak impact model fails most categories and the reference has no high or critical findings.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: MCP server and agent skills

docs.title: Reports and Decks
docs.text: Every report, deck, and table is built from the same view of the impact model, so a number or a label never differs between artifacts. The output is deterministic: the same inputs give byte-identical files.

docs.title: Definition reports
docs.text:
These describe the impact model and need no observations, so a workshop can review them before any data exists.

impact-model report logic-model impact-model.yaml --pathway pw-supply
impact-model report definitions impact-model.yaml --out definitions.md
Kind What it shows pathway The causal pathways, as diagrams logic-model Inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes for each pathway. --diagram draws it left to right (also logic-model-diagram) logic-model-layered The logic model as columns, from inputs to impact, with a box for each item and an arrow wherever the impact model says one leads to another. Written as Mermaid logic-model-d2 The same layered diagram as D2, where a grid keeps every stage in its own column. Render it with d2 diagram.d2 diagram.svg problem-tree The core problem with its causes below and effects above, arrows flowing upward, and tables of what addresses each. Written as Mermaid; see the problem tree guide problem-tree-d2 The same problem tree as D2, where a grid keeps every row in place problem-tree-json The diagram document the problem tree is drawn from: a d2vision diagram spec, as JSON, with no stamp outcome-map The outcomes framework, marking what is monitored but not owned logframe A results-framework matrix with indicators, means of verification, and assumptions metrics Metric definitions and how they combine across pathways metric-selection Candidate indicators scored against your criteria, best first collection-plan What is collected, how, how often, and the burden against the budget glossary The words the impact model uses assessment How much of the impact model is stated, inferred, or still a hypothesis definitions All of the above as one document

docs.title: Status reports
docs.text:
These need observations (-O) and describe how far the impact model has come.

impact-model report exec impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml --prev status-q2.json
impact-model report story impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml --audience aud-funders
impact-model report learning-review impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml --period 2026-Q3
Kind What it shows exec The executive summary: where things stand and what changed results Indicator and outcome results, separating what the organization answers for from what it only monitors assumptions The assumption register and what moved interventions Each intervention and what it is delivering evidence-gaps Where claims rest on weak or missing evidence full Every status report in one document story An update for one audience (--audience), using the numbers and consented stories headline The numbers each audience is told, from its headline list, with the latest figure, status, and caveats (--audience narrows it to one) metric-tree Per pathway: its North Star and guardrails, then its indicators from activity to impact, as a table and a diagram (--pathway narrows it) learning-review A period's review (--period): what changed, surprises, decisions portfolio Pathways side by side, described without recommending narrative The impact model as prose, checking the solution against the problem actors Who does what, including partners custom Your own Go text/template over the report view (--template)

narrative, actors, and custom also work without observations.

docs.title: Consent and sensitivity
docs.text: Stories and quotes are gated. A story appears only if consent was granted, and a quote only if its sensitivity is public or internal. Evidence marked restricted is never rendered: its excerpt, summary, and URL are withheld from every report, deck, and judge bundle, since a URL can reveal where a confidential document lives.

docs.title: Slide decks
docs.text:
impact-model deck workshop impact-model.yaml -o workshop.md
impact-model deck exec impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml --export exec.pdf
Deck Contents workshop The problem, the goal and ceiling, a diagram, a logic model table, and the logic model drawn as columns with arrows per pathway, key assumptions, metric definitions, the glossary, and what is still our reading. Needs no observations exec Where we stand, and what changed since the last snapshot (--prev) learning-review Behind plan, what we decided, and questions for discussion (--period) story One audience's deck: what you told us you need, the numbers, what we ask of you (--audience)

A deck is written as Marp Markdown. With --export file (.pdf, .pptx, or .html) it is also rendered by marp, and by mmdc when it has diagrams. Each deck carries speaker notes and shows the export stamp (impact model, version, and hash) on its title slide.

docs.title: Word and PowerPoint
docs.text:
impact-model export docx definitions impact-model.yaml --out impact-model.docx --reference-doc template.docx
impact-model export pptx workshop impact-model.yaml --out workshop.pptx

These convert the Markdown to a Pandoc-ready profile (diagrams as PNG, basis badges as text, page breaks) and run mmdc and pandoc. --reference-doc styles the output with your own template. If a tool is missing, nothing is written and the exit code is 3.

docs.title: Spreadsheets
docs.text:
impact-model export csv indicators impact-model.yaml --out indicators.csv

Tables: indicators, metrics, glossary, metric-selection, and collection-plan. The files follow RFC 4180. Multi-valued cells are joined with ;.

docs.title: The export stamp
docs.text: Every export starts with a stamp, model:<id> version:<v> hash:<h>, where the hash is of the impact model's canonical form. The same hash appears in every format, so you can tell that a PDF, a Word file, and a spreadsheet came from the same version. --no-stamp leaves it off, and --as-of records the date the artifact describes.

docs.title: PRISM exports
docs.text:
impact-model export okr impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml -o okr.json
impact-model export journey impact-model.yaml -o journeys.json
impact-model export v2mom impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml -o v2mom.json
impact-model export dmaic impact-model.yaml -O obs-q3.yaml -o dmaic.json

export okr turns each owned outcome that has measured indicators into an objective, with each indicator as a key result carrying baseline, target, current value, score, status, and confidence. export journey writes outcome journeys. export v2mom writes a V2MOM with one method per pathway; the V2MOM guide maps each part. export dmaic writes a DMAIC metrics document for the pathways marked for DMAIC; the DMAIC guide maps each part. All four are JSON for the PRISM tools.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Review round trip

docs.title: The layered logic model diagram
docs.text:
logic-model --diagram draws each stage as a group and joins the groups, which says only that one stage follows another. The layered diagram draws the real relationships:

  • an input leads to the activities that use it, and one input can feed several;
  • an activity leads to the outputs it lists, which lead on to the outcomes it targets;
  • an outcome leads to the outcomes its causal links point to, so one box can lead to several, and several can lead to one.

The order within a column is chosen to keep arrows from crossing. A link that runs back to an earlier stage is feedback. It is left out of the diagram, where it would cut across the boxes between, and listed under it.

Both diagrams are available, so you can compare them. The layered one is made by pkg/logicmodel, which builds a layered graph from the impact model and writes it through d2vision's diagram spec, the same spec that writes the D2 and the Mermaid.

docs.title: Review Round Trip
docs.text:
An impact model is only as good as the people who have read it. The round trip sends it out for review, brings the answers back as proposed changes you can inspect, and records approval. Nothing changes the impact model until you apply it.

export packet or sheet  ->  reviewers answer  ->  import review  ->  apply patch  ->  approve

docs.title: 1. Send it out
docs.text:
Two formats carry the same rows, one per element:

impact-model export review-packet impact-model.yaml --format docx --out packet.docx   # for reviewers who work in a document
impact-model export review-sheet impact-model.yaml --out sheet.csv                    # for reviewers who work in a spreadsheet

Each row has the element's ID, its statement, its basis, and its sources, with empty Decision, Suggested change, and Comment columns. Rejected elements are not put to reviewers. Sources are named by ID and title only; excerpts and URLs are never included.

The decision is one of agree, change, remove, or unsure. Both formats carry the export stamp, so a reply can be matched to the version it answers.

docs.title: 2. Collect the answers
docs.text: Reviewers fill in the packet or the sheet and return it. You can also write the answers as a ReviewResponse file (see impact-model schema review-response). How the files travel (email, a shared drive, a form) is up to you.

docs.title: 3. Bring them back
docs.text:
impact-model import review impact-model.yaml --from-csv returned-sheet.csv \
  --reviewer "Program board" --date 2026-06-15 \
  --out review.patch.json --consultation-out consultation.json

The impact model is never changed. The command writes a patch of the changes it could work out, a list of the rows that need a person to decide, and a consultation record of the review. A row is handled like this:

Decision What happens agree The element's basis becomes confirmed remove The element's basis becomes rejected change If the suggestion is field: value lines, those fields are set. Free text is flagged for a person unsure, or a comment with no decision Flagged

A row with no element ID is matched to an element by its quoted text, and flagged if no single element matches. If the answers were written against a different version of the impact model (the hash differs), every row is flagged.

docs.title: 4. Apply what you accept
docs.text:
impact-model patch impact-model.yaml review.patch.json --dry-run
impact-model patch impact-model.yaml review.patch.json

Review the patch first. It goes through the same validated path as every other edit.

docs.title: 5. Approve
docs.text:
impact-model approve impact-model.yaml --version 1.0.0 --date 2026-07-01 \
  --approver "Board chair:chair" --approver "Executive director:director"

Approval sets the status to approved, sets the version label, and appends a revision naming the approvers. It is refused, with nothing written, if the impact model has validation errors; if elements are still hypotheses (confirm or reject them, or use --force with --reason, which is recorded); or if the version label is missing or already used, the date is missing, or there is no approver. Use a name or role you are happy to publish.

docs.title: Sharing through Google Docs and Sheets
docs.text: The packet and the sheet are ordinary files, so any shared drive works. To use Google Docs and Sheets, the gogoogle command line can upload the packet as a Google Doc (gogoogle drive upload packet.docx --convert doc), list its comments (gogoogle drive comments), show reviewers' suggested edits (gogoogle docs suggestions), and read a returned sheet as records (gogoogle sheets records). This tool makes no network calls itself. An agent skill that runs that whole workflow is planned.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Quality and judging

docs.title: V2MOM
docs.text:
If you already write V2MOMs, this page shows where each part of a V2MOM comes from in an impact model, and what the impact model adds that a V2MOM written by hand usually leaves out.

impact-model export v2mom impact-model.yaml -O observations.yaml -o v2mom.json

The output is a V2MOM document in the JSON format of prism-roadmap's goals/v2mom package, which validates it and can render it as slides.

docs.title: The mapping at a glance
docs.text:
V2MOM Comes from In impact model terms Vision context.vision The future the organization works toward Values context.values, in order The principles that guide how it works, most important first Methods pathways, one method each A pathway is a program, product, or strategy: a group of outcomes and the interventions that bring them about A method's projects the pathway's interventionIds An intervention is something the organization does to change an outcome, such as a coaching program or a feature launch A method's measures the pathway's focus: North Star, one metric that matters, guardrails The few indicators the program steers by Obstacles risks, and high or critical assumptions not yet shown to hold What could stop the plan A method's owner the pathway's ownerActorId The actor who answers for the pathway

The sections below explain each row. Two rules hold throughout:

  • Nothing is invented. Every field in the V2MOM is copied or translated from something in the impact model. A section the model cannot fill is left empty, and a V2MOM that would fail validation is refused instead of written.
  • Order is kept. Values, methods, measures, and projects appear in the order the impact model lists them, so the same model always gives the same V2MOM.

docs.title: One pathway, end to end
docs.text:
This pathway from the fictional intermediary example is a program called Learning Exchange:

pathways:
  - id: pw-learning
    title: Learning Exchange
    kind: program
    description: Peer learning and leadership coaching for member leaders.
    ownerActorId: act-network
    outcomeIds: [oc-out-cohorts, oc-st-leader-skills, oc-st-peer-ties, oc-im-leaders-practice, oc-im-peer-network]
    interventionIds: [int-peer-cohorts, int-leader-coaching, int-training-series]
    focus:
      northStarId: ind-practice-maturity
      guardrailIds: [ind-retention-learning]

It becomes this method, shown trimmed, with observations as of 2026-09-30:

{
  "id": "pw-learning",
  "name": "Learning Exchange",
  "description": "Peer learning and leadership coaching for member leaders.",
  "owner": "Riverbend Nonprofit Network",
  "measures": [
    {
      "id": "ind-practice-maturity",
      "name": "Leadership practice maturity",
      "description": "North Star: Median level of participating members on the four-step leadership practice rubric, rated by a coach and the member together.",
      "baseline": "Emerging",
      "target": "Established",
      "current": "Emerging",
      "timeline": "2028-12-31",
      "status": "On Track"
    }
  ],
  "obstacles": [
    { "id": "rsk-time-burden", "name": "Leaders drop out of cohorts because they cannot spare the time." },
    { "id": "asm-skills-applied", "name": "Leaders put coaching-based skills into practice back at their organizations." }
  ],
  "projects": ["int-peer-cohorts", "int-leader-coaching", "int-training-series"]
}
  • The pathway's title, description, and owner become the method's.
  • The North Star leads the measures, and the guardrail follows it (trimmed here).
  • The three interventions become the method's projects, each also listed in the V2MOM's project list with "methodId": "pw-learning".
  • A risk that applies to the cohorts, and a critical assumption about leaders applying their skills, become the method's obstacles.
  • The five outcomes and the links between them are not in the V2MOM. They are the reasoning behind the method, and report pathway draws them.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
The V2MOM's vision is context.vision, word for word.

context:
  vision: A county where every resident can count on a strong local nonprofit when they need one.

The impact model also has context.mission, why the organization exists. A V2MOM has no mission section, so the mission is not exported.

docs.title: Values
docs.text:
The V2MOM's values are context.values. The first value has priority 1, the next priority 2, and so on.

context:
  values:
    - name: Members first
      description: Every program answers to what member nonprofits need, not to what is easy to offer.
    - name: Stronger together
      description: Shared services and a shared voice do more than each organization can alone.

Values frame the model, like the mission and vision. They are not outcomes: nothing in the model causes them, and they are not measured.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Each pathway becomes one method, in the order the model lists them. A pathway is the impact model's unit of "how we will get there": a program, product, or strategy, with its own outcomes, its own interventions, and its own owner. A V2MOM usually has three to seven methods, and a model usually has a similar number of pathways.

Method field From the pathway ID id Name title Description description Owner the name of the actor in ownerActorId

A pathway marked rejected, such as a program the organization decided against, is not exported.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
A method's projects are the pathway's interventions, the things the organization does. They are listed once in the V2MOM's project list, each with the ID of the method it belongs to.

Project field From the intervention ID, Name, Description id, title, description Method the pathway it is listed in Status planned → Approved, in_progress → In Progress, completed → Completed, cancelled → Cancelled; paused is left blank External links initiativeRefs, keyed by framework, such as a Jira or VisionStudio item

"Intervention" is the impact model's word because the model is causal: each intervention says which outcomes it should change. An initiative is the organizational effort that delivers one, and initiativeRefs links the two.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
A method's measures are the indicators the pathway steers by, from its focus:

  1. the North Star, the one number that best shows the value the program delivers
  2. the one metric that matters, if the pathway names one for now
  3. the guardrails, which watch what pursuing the North Star could harm

Each measure's description starts with its role, such as "North Star:".

Measure field From the indicator ID, Name, Unit id, name, unit Description the role, then definition Baseline baseline Target, Timeline the latest-dated target and its date Current, Progress, Status the indicator's status, only when observations are given with -O

Status is On Track, At Risk, Behind, or Achieved, from the indicator's state on the status date. A pathway without a focus exports a method with no measures; impact-model lint points out programs and products that have no North Star.

The V2MOM has no top-level measures. Every measure belongs to a method, which the document records as the nested structure.

docs.title: Obstacles
docs.text:
Obstacles come from two places:

  • Risks: things that could go wrong. Impact becomes severity, probability becomes likelihood, and the mitigation and status carry over.
  • Assumptions the plan depends on that could still turn out false: those with high or critical criticality whose status is untested, at risk, or invalidated. With observations (-O), an assumption's assessed status is used, so one assessed as holding drops out and one assessed as at risk comes in. Without them, the status written in the model is used, and an assumption with no status counts as untested. The obstacle's severity is the assumption's criticality, and its description says how the assumption will be tested.

An obstacle that applies to one of a pathway's outcomes, interventions, or the links between them is listed under that method. One that applies across pathways, or to nothing in particular, is listed for the whole V2MOM.

docs.title: What a V2MOM leaves out
docs.text:
A V2MOM is a short plan, so the export keeps only what fits it. These parts of the impact model are not in the V2MOM, and other projections show them:

Left out Where to see it The outcomes and the causal links between them report pathway, the theory of change Every assumption, with its test, evidence, and status report assumptions Indicators other than a pathway's focus report metric-tree What each audience is told report headline Where each element came from: stated, inferred, or confirmed report assessment The mission context.mission in the model

docs.title: What the impact model adds
docs.text:
A V2MOM written by hand often states its methods and measures without saying why the methods should lead to the vision. Exported from an impact model:

  • each method is backed by a pathway of outcomes, each link with its reason
  • each North Star is one that impact-model lint has checked sits at or below the organization's ceiling of accountability, so the V2MOM does not commit the organization to change it cannot answer for
  • the obstacles include the assumptions the plan rests on, not only external risks
  • with -O, the measures carry the latest observed values and status

docs.title: When the export is refused
docs.text:
A V2MOM needs a vision, at least one value, and at least one method. If the impact model has no context.vision, no context.values, or no pathway, export v2mom writes nothing and exits with status 2, naming what to add:

impact-model: impact-model.yaml: the impact model cannot be drawn as a V2MOM: add context.values

Add values with a patch:

impact-model patch impact-model.yaml - <<'EOF'
[{"op":"add","path":"/context/values","value":[
  {"name":"Members first","description":"Every program answers to what members need."}]}]
EOF

docs.title: Going the other way
docs.text: There is no import from a V2MOM. A V2MOM has no outcomes, causal links, or assumptions to read, so an impact model built from one would have to invent the reasoning that makes it an impact model. Start the impact model from the V2MOM's vision, values, and methods instead: each method suggests a pathway, and each measure an indicator.

docs.title: Integration contract for USM and UFM
docs.text:
This page says what the impact model module promises to the Unified Strategy Model (USM) and the Unified Futures Model (UFM), and what it asks of them. It is a contract in the plain sense: each side can build against it without reading the other's code.

Status: draft, for review by the owners of USM and UFM. Nothing here is final until they have read it.

docs.title: What each model uses an impact model for
docs.text:
• USM describes a strategy from one market participant's point of view, combining a theory of change with a balanced scorecard. It reads a Impact model's outcomes, indicators, status, and confidence, and attaches its own scorecard measures to elements of the impact model.
  • UFM describes competing futures of a market, such as one scheme winning over another. It groups impact models by the future each one is working toward and compares them.

The impact model is the shared part: neither model owns it, and it owns neither of them.

docs.title: 1. Every impact model and element has a stable address
docs.text:
An impact model is model:<doc>; an element is model:<doc>#<element>. Both parts are slugs: lower case letters, digits, and single hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 128 characters. An ID is permanent for the life of the element:

  • the tools never change an element's ID (impact-model outcome set refuses to), and impact-model patch addresses elements by ID, not position;
  • renaming means removing the element and adding a new one, which shows as such in impact-model diff;
  • a removed or rejected element keeps its place in history, and its ID should not be reused for something else.

USM and UFM should store these references, not copies of the content.

docs.title: 2. An impact model says whose it is and which future it belongs to
docs.text:
perspective:
  actorId: act-open-group          # the market participant (USM's participant)
  role: proponent                  # proponent | funder | implementer | observer
  futureRef: ufm:open-standard-wins   # the future (UFM's future)

futureRef has the form ufm:<slug>. UFM owns what a future is; the impact model only points at it. Two impact models may belong to the same future if they speak for different actors; two impact models may not speak for the same actor in the same future (impact-model validate --futures reports it).

docs.title: 3. Impact models in one market share actors through a registry
docs.text:
An ActorRegistry document holds the actors several impact models refer to. A Impact model names it in actorRegistry, and actor IDs not defined in the impact model resolve there. The tools check that competing futures name one registry (validate --registry actors.yaml --futures).

USM and UFM may read the registry to learn who the market's actors are. They should not add actors to a registry belonging to an impact model they do not own; add them to their own and have the impact model reference both.

docs.title: 4. Strategy data attaches by alignment, and the impact model never holds it
docs.text:
An impact model may carry alignments: an element ID and an external target (framework, ref, relation). Frameworks include bsc, usm, ufm, okr, v2mom, and market_spec. This is how a scorecard objective or measure points at an outcome or indicator.

The impact model never stores scorecard data. USM computes its scorecard from the Impact model's status and its own measures. The impact model does not list the models that consume it: references run from USM and UFM into the impact model.

docs.title: 5. Status is a document
docs.text:
impact-model status produces a ImpactModelStatus document (schema impact-model-status) that anyone can read without the Go module. For each indicator, outcome, link, and assumption it gives a state; for each outcome, a pathway state and a confidence from 0 to 1; and, per impact outcome, the headline. The snapshot records the settings it was computed with, so any number can be traced, and the same inputs always give the same bytes.

USM should read states and confidence from the snapshot instead of recomputing them. A change in how status is computed is a change to the module's version and is listed in its changelog.

docs.title: 6. Comparing futures
docs.text: Competing-futures impact models compare without any schema change: see examples/competing-futures. A UFM reading three impact models can line up their impact outcomes (each is level: impact), their status and confidence, and the assumptions each depends on. An impact model may name another impact model's element in an alignment or an indicator's external reference; validate --futures checks that such a reference resolves.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
• Documents carry specVersion (currently 0.1). A change that makes a valid document invalid, or renames a field or an enumeration value, raises it.
  • The JSON Schemas are published under schema/v0/ and are generated from the Go types, which are the source of truth.
  • Additive changes (a new optional field, a new element kind) do not raise the version. Readers should ignore fields they do not know.
  • The reference grammar and the futureRef form are part of this contract and change only with a major version.

docs.title: How a model reads an impact model
docs.text:
Any of these, in order of preference for a program:

  1. The Go packages: pkg/impact (types), pkg/impactio (read and write), pkg/measure (status), pkg/report (views).
  2. The command line, with --format json where offered.
  3. The MCP server (impact-model mcp), which exposes validate, lint, graph, status, report, patch, deck, judge bundle, and diff to an agent.
  4. The files and schemas alone.

docs.title: What the module does not do
docs.text:
• It does not model a market, a scorecard, or a future. Those belong to USM and UFM.
  • It does not call them, and it does not depend on them.
  • It does not decide which future is more likely; it states, for each, what has to be true and how well that is supported.

docs.title: Open questions for the owners
docs.text:
1. Does USM want the impact model's alignments to be one-way (USM points at the Impact model) only, or may an impact model point at a scorecard objective, as bsc alignments do today?
  2. Is ufm:<slug> the right form for a future's reference, or should UFM publish its own reference grammar for the module to adopt?
  3. Should confidence be offered to UFM as a number, as now, or only as high, medium, and low?
  4. Which of the status snapshot's fields does USM need that are not there?

docs.text: See CHANGELOG.md for the full changelog.
