docs.title: 6.4 Lint rules (initial set)
docs.text:
Severity error blocks GO; warning is reported; info is advisory.

Rule ID Severity Check IMP-STR-001 error At least one outcome with level impact IMP-STR-002 error No unintended cycles (cycles not marked feedback) IMP-STR-003 error Every non-impact outcome has a path to an impact outcome (no dead ends) IMP-STR-004 warning Every outcome has ≥ 1 precondition or a targeting intervention (no orphans) IMP-STR-005 warning at_least logic has k between 1 and number of preconditions IMP-STR-006 warning Links respect level order (no link from a higher level to a lower level unless feedback; same-level links allowed) IMP-STR-007 warning Precondition groups are well-formed: ≥ 2 members, every member has a link into the group's target, no group cycles. (A nested group must target the same outcome as the group containing it; this part is a validation error, VAL-GRP-004.) IMP-MET-003 warning A weighted_mean metric's weight metric is instantiated by an indicator in every pathway that uses the weighted metric, so the roll-up can be computed IMP-PTH-003 info pathway.outcomeIds agree with the pathwayIds of the indicators measuring those outcomes IMP-LOG-004 info Outcomes with ≥ 2 incoming links state their logic explicitly (non-default logic or a group), per Davies' AND/OR ambiguity critique IMP-LOG-001 warning Every causal link into a medium_term, long_term, or impact outcome has a rationale IMP-LOG-002 warning Every link into an outcome above short_term has ≥ 1 linked assumption IMP-LOG-003 info Impact outcomes have ≥ 2 preconditions (single-chain theories are usually incomplete) IMP-ASM-001 warning Every high/critical assumption has a test description IMP-ASM-002 warning Every high/critical assumption cites evidence (assessments live in observation sets, which lint does not read) IMP-ASM-003 info At least one contextual or external assumption exists IMP-MEA-001 error When a ceiling of accountability is declared (IMP-ACC-001 asks for one), every outcome within it is measured: it has ≥ 1 indicator, or is named in another indicator's proxyFor IMP-MEA-002 warning Every indicator has baseline, ≥ 1 target, data source, and frequency IMP-MEA-003 warning Quantitative indicators have a unit and direction IMP-MEA-004 warning Target dates fall within the document's time horizon IMP-MEA-005 warning Timeline consistency: an outcome's final target date is not earlier than the final target dates of its preconditions IMP-ACC-002 warning Outcomes above the ceiling of accountability are not explicitly marked responsibility: own (the organization contributes to them, it does not own them) IMP-INT-001 error Every intervention targets ≥ 1 outcome (enforced by validation as VAL-INT-001, so it is never reached by lint) IMP-INT-002 warning Every intervention has an owner actor IMP-ACC-001 warning A ceiling of accountability is declared IMP-ACT-001 info Outcomes in the influence sphere name ≥ 1 actor (boundary partner) IMP-EVD-001 info Links into impact-level outcomes cite ≥ 1 evidence record IMP-PTH-001 warning Every pathway contains ≥ 1 outcome with a path to an impact outcome IMP-PTH-002 info Every pathway has ≥ 1 selected indicator IMP-MET-001 warning Every common-layer metric is instantiated by an indicator in every pathway, or the omission is explained in the indicator selection rationale IMP-MET-002 error rollupFrom is only used when the metric's aggregation is not none, and all roll-up sources instantiate the same metric (enforced by validation as VAL-MET-002, so it is never reached by lint) IMP-CLM-001 warning Indicators measuring outcomes above the ceiling of accountability claim contribution, not attribution IMP-BUD-001 warning Selected indicators' staff minutes per week ≤ measurementBudget.staffMinutesPerWeek IMP-BUD-002 warning Survey / form questions per respondent per year ≤ maxQuestionsPerRespondentPerYear IMP-BUD-003 info Number of selected indicators within targetSelectedMetrics IMP-BUD-004 info Selected indicators declare collection.mode; passive and derived preferred over survey where an equivalent exists (reported as share passive) IMP-AUD-001 info Every audience is targeted by ≥ 1 selected indicator or story theme IMP-CAU-001 warning Every underlying and structural cause is addressed by ≥ 1 outcome or marked outOfScope with a reason IMP-CAU-002 info When causes are declared, outcomes address ≥ 1 non-immediate cause (root causes, not only immediate ones) IMP-CAU-003 warning A cause contributes only to causes at its own level or nearer the problem (structural → underlying → immediate); a parent at a deeper level usually means the link was written backwards IMP-RSP-001 warning Outcomes with responsibility partner or shared name ≥ 1 delivering actor; shared names ≥ 2 IMP-RSP-002 info partner and unaddressed outcomes on a path to impact still have ≥ 1 indicator (monitor the whole solution tree) IMP-ASM-004 warning Assumptions with needsTesting: true have a test and either a monitoring indicator or a linked decision / evaluation question IMP-ASM-005 info Assumptions of type partnership exist when any outcome is shared or partner IMP-RSK-001 info high / critical assumptions have ≥ 1 related risk with mitigation IMP-EQU-001 warning Indicators on outcomes that target groups disaggregate by those groups (specify changes for target groups, not assume them) IMP-VAL-001 info Each of focus, change_analysis, assumptions_risks, actors has ≥ 1 consultation record IMP-PRV-001 warning (full profile only) Every element declares a provenance basis IMP-PRV-002 warning Every stated element cites ≥ 1 evidence record with a URL or document reference IMP-PRV-003 warning An approved document has no hypothesis elements at accountable levels (responsibility own or shared) IMP-PRV-004 info Selected indicators declare dataAvailability IMP-DMA-001 warning An indicator of a pathway marked projections: [dmaic] declares a frequency and a data source (dataSource or collection.system) IMP-DMA-002 warning An indicator of a DMAIC pathway is measured ≥ 20 times a year, so control limits can be set within about a year IMP-DMA-003 warning A survey indicator of a DMAIC pathway gets ≥ 30 responses per measurement (collection.respondentsPerYear × sampleRate ÷ measurements per year), and states respondentsPerYear IMP-EFF-001 warning Every effect is relieved by ≥ 1 outcome (addressesEffects) or marked outOfScope with a reason IMP-EFF-002 info Outcomes that relieve effects include ≥ 1 at long_term or impact level (effects are what the program ultimately reduces; causes are what it works on)

Rule IDs are permanent. Retired rules keep their ID reserved.

docs.title: 6.5 Measurement algorithms
docs.text:
Indicator progress (quantitative). With baseline b, current c, final target t, direction d:

  • increase: p = (c − b) / (t − b); decrease: p = (b − c) / (b − t).
  • maintain: p = 1 if |c − t| ≤ tolerance else 0.
  • If t = b, p = 1 when the target condition holds, else 0.
  • p is clamped to [0, 1.5] for display; achieved when p ≥ 1.

Expected progress at asOf. Targets form a time series (baseline.date, 0) → (target_i.date, p_i). Expected e is linear interpolation at asOf (0 before the baseline date, 1 after the final target). Indicator status:

Condition Status no targets defined (baseline only) baseline_only (latest value reported, no progress computed) no observation and asOf < first target date not_started no observation and asOf ≥ first target date no_data last observation older than 2 × frequency stale p ≥ 1 achieved p ≥ e − tol (default tol = 0.10) on_track p ≥ e − 2·tol at_risk otherwise off_track

Qualitative indicators use the ordinal position of the observed level in the indicator's ordered levels as c, with b and t as level positions.

Health mapping (prism-core): achieved, on_track → green; at_risk, stale → yellow; off_track → red; not_started, no_data, baseline_only → no health (rendered grey). baseline_only ranks with not_started in roll-ups.

Metric roll-ups. For an indicator with rollupFrom, the value at a date is computed from the latest source observations at or before that date using the metric's aggregation (weighted_mean weights by the latest value of weightMetricId's indicator in the same pathway). If any source lacks a value the roll-up is no_data and lists the missing sources. Direct observations of a roll-up indicator take precedence and the computed value is reported alongside for comparison.

Theme counts. A theme_count indicator's value for a period is the number of stories in that period's observation sets tagged with any of its themeIds (optionally filtered by pathwayIds); stories are counted once.

Collection burden (pkg/burden). Per selected indicator, staff minutes are normalized to minutes per week from collection.minutesPerPeriod and collection.period; respondent questions per year = questionsPerRespondent × (collections per year) × sampleRate. Totals are reported overall, per pathway, and per mode; budget comparisons feed TOC-BUD-*.

Outcome status = roll-up of its indicators by Rollup option: worst (default) or mean of progress. Outcomes without indicators get unmeasured.

Pathway status. Processed in topological order from the leaves upward. A node's precondition signal is computed over incoming non-feedback links: grouped sources are first reduced through their PreconditionGroup (nested groups innermost first), then the group results and ungrouped sources are combined with the outcome's logic: all → worst; any → best; at_least k → k-th best. Status ordering for worst/best is off_track < at_risk < stale < no_data < not_started < on_track < achieved. Pathway status = worse of (own outcome status, precondition signal), where unmeasured defers to the precondition signal.

Assumption propagation. Effective assumption status = latest assessment in observation sets, else the document's static status. A link whose assumptions include invalidated is broken; at_risk makes it at_risk. Every outcome downstream of a broken link gets the flag assumptionBroken: [assumptionIDs] and its pathway status is capped at at_risk (critical assumption: off_track).

Link confidence ∈ [0, 1]: 0.4·evidence + 0.4·assumptions + 0.2·rationale, where evidence = max strength of supporting evidence (strong 1.0, moderate 0.7, weak 0.4, anecdotal 0.2, none 0) minus half the max strength of contradicting evidence, floored at 0, assumptions = min over linked assumption statuses (validated 1.0, holding 0.8, untested 0.5, at_risk 0.25, invalidated 0), and rationale = 1 if present else 0. Path confidence = product of link confidences along the path; an outcome's confidence = max over its paths to impact. Weights are options with these defaults and are printed in every report that shows a confidence value (INV-5).

Diff. Diff(prev, cur) lists status changes for indicators, outcomes, assumptions, and pathways, ordered per INV-3.

docs.title: 6.6 Reports
docs.text:
Kind Content exec Headline (goal, overall pathway status, as-of), status by level, top 5 at-risk / off-track outcomes with driving indicators, broken or untested critical assumptions, changes since previous snapshot, decisions requested (from Model.decisions and auto-generated prompts for broken assumptions), confidence footnote pathway Mermaid flowchart BT with subgraphs by level, nodes styled by health, dashed feedback links, ceiling of accountability as a subgraph boundary results Results framework: outcome → indicator → baseline → targets → latest → status assumptions Assumption register: statement, type, criticality, applies to, test, evidence, status interventions Intervention → owner → status → targeted outcomes → pathway status evidence-gaps Links and critical assumptions lacking evidence; outcomes lacking indicators story For one --audience: audience needs, the indicators and outcomes tagged for it with latest values and status, consented stories tagged for it (summary always; quote only per TRD-023), theme counts, and caveats — a narrative scaffold for communications staff to finish learning-review For a period: status changes since previous snapshot, largest deviations from expected progress (surprises), assumption status changes, theme counts and new themes, data-quality notes, and draft questions; merges any recorded LearningReview for the period portfolio Per pathway: pathway status, outcome-status distribution, confidence, collection burden, share of passive data, audiences covered, and open decisions — evidence for grow / adjust / sunset decisions, without a recommendation narrative Programme / strategy document scaffold following the UNDG section mapping (research §9.7): causal analysis (problem tree → outcomes addressing each cause level), priorities and rationale (priority scores), assumptions and risks with mitigation, partner-delivered and unaddressed elements, implementation arrangements (who does what), M&E provisions (assumptions needing testing, monitoring cadence, evaluation questions from evidence gaps), validation trail (consultations), key messages. Works without observations; adds status when given assessment Definition-phase assessment (no observations needed): provenance mix with lists, outcomes without indicators, indicators by data availability, assumptions needing testing, open decisions, generated questions for the organization, short narrative summary. Inferred and hypothesis elements are marked in every report and deck by a basis badge actors Division of labour: actors × outcomes / interventions with roles; outcomes needing collaboration; outcomes with no delivering actor; partner-delivered outcomes being monitored full All status reports in one document custom User text/template over report.View

Definition reports (no observations required):

Kind Content pathway As above, without status styling when no status is given; --pathway restricts to one pathway plus its route to impact logic-model --diagram adds a left-to-right Mermaid flow of the same stages. Per pathway: inputs (intervention resources) → activities (interventions) → outputs (output-level outcomes and intervention outputs) → outcomes (short / medium / long-term) → impact, as a table outcome-map The outcomes framework: per pathway, outcomes grouped by level from impact down, each with sphere, category, change type, responsibility and delivering actors, the causes it addresses, and its indicators; outcomes above the ceiling of accountability and monitored-only outcomes are marked logframe Logframe matrix per pathway: rows goal (impact), purpose (long-term and medium-term outcomes), outputs (short-term and output outcomes), activities (interventions); columns narrative, indicators with targets, means of verification (indicator data source and method), and assumptions (those applying to the row's links and interventions) metrics Metric definitions: name, definition, formula, unit, aggregation, layer, and which pathways instantiate each metric-selection Candidate indicators × selection criteria with weighted score, status, rationale; sorted by score collection-plan Selected indicators: definition, source system, mode, owner, frequency, minutes per period, questions per respondent; totals vs budget glossary Glossary terms and theme codebook problem-tree Markdown: the problem tree as a Mermaid flowchart BT (causes in rows below the core problem, effects in rows above, arrows upward), then a table of causes and one of effects, each with its level or parents and the outcomes that address it or why it is set aside problem-tree-d2 The same diagram in D2, whose grid keeps each row in place problem-tree-json The diagram document itself: the d2vision diagram spec (nodes with row, edges) that problem-tree and problem-tree-d2 are rendered from definitions All definition reports in one document (the workshop pack)

Problem tree layering: the core problem is row 0. A cause with no parents is in row −1; any other cause is one row below its lowest parent (row = min(parent rows) − 1), so every arrow from a cause points up. Effects mirror this upward: an effect with no parents is in row +1, any other is one row above its highest parent. Rejected causes and effects are left out. Within a row, nodes keep file order.

report.View is a documented, versioned struct (ViewVersion = "1"); changing field names is a breaking change.

docs.title: 6.7 Reference grammar (pkg/ref)
docs.text:
ref      = "model:" docSlug [ "#" elementId ]
docSlug  = slug                ; e.g. model:agent-auth-open-standard
elementId= slug                ; e.g. model:agent-auth-open-standard#oc-idp-support
slug     = [a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*    ; ≤ 128 chars

Element IDs inside a document are slugs (INV-1). External references use ExternalRef { framework, ref, url?, relation }; ref is opaque to this module (for market-spec it is that repo's {type}:{slug} form). This grammar is the USM/UFM integration contract together with §7.3.

docs.title: 6.8 Error Semantics
docs.text: Not applicable as HTTP — there is no network API. CLI exit codes are in §6.1. MCP tool errors return isError: true with a JSON body { code, message, issues? }; codes mirror sentinel errors (invalid_document, unknown_reference, unsupported_format, path_outside_root).

docs.title: 6.9 Versioning
docs.text:
• Schema $id: https://github.com/ProductBuildersHQ/impact-model/schema/v0/<name>.schema.json.
  • Every document carries kind (ImpactModel | ObservationSet | ImpactModelStatus) and specVersion ("0.1").
  • Within v0.x, minor versions are additive; removals or renames require a major bump and a migration note in the CHANGELOG.

docs.title: 6.10 Events
docs.text: Not applicable — no event bus; file outputs only.

docs.title: 6.11 CSV mapping and agent skills
docs.text:
CSV mapping file (YAML, schema-defined as csv-mapping):

modelId: example-network
columns:
  indicator: metric_id        # column holding indicator ID, or…
  indicatorFixed: ""          # …a fixed indicator ID for single-indicator sheets
  date: period_end
  value: value
  pathway: program_area       # optional
  quality: data_quality       # optional
  source: source              # optional
indicatorAliases:             # map spreadsheet labels to indicator IDs
  "Attendee hours": ind-attendee-hours
dateFormat: "2006-01-02"

Rows whose indicator, date, or value cannot be resolved are written to the unmatched list with row number and reason (INV-4).

Agent skills (skills/<name>/SKILL.md plus templates). Each skill states purpose, inputs, the exact command sequence, checks to report, and outputs. AI judgment is limited to drafting text and asking the user; every number comes from a command.

Skill Command sequence (abridged) Checks reported impact-author impact-model init → edit → impact-model validate → impact-model lint → impact-model report definitions validation issues, lint GO/NO-GO, definition pack written impact-status-refresh impact-model import observations --csv → impact-model validate → impact-model status --prev → impact-model report exec rows imported / unmatched, indicators with new data, changes vs previous snapshot impact-learning-review impact-model status → impact-model report learning-review → assistant drafts discussion questions surprises listed, assumptions changed impact-audience-story impact-model report story --audience → assistant drafts narrative from the scaffold every number in the draft present in the scaffold; no unconsented quotes impact-draft-from-sources impact-model init → for each source: assistant reads it, impact-model evidence add --url … --excerpt … → assistant proposes elements → impact-model patch (each element with provenance.basis and evidenceIds) → impact-model validate → impact-model lint --profile draft → impact-model report definitions and impact-model report assessment sources recorded, elements by basis, stated elements without citation (must be 0), lint GO under draft toc-share-google impact-model export review-packet --format docx, impact-model export review-sheet, impact-model deck … --export / impact-model export pptx → upload with conversion (gogoogle CLI drive upload --convert) → after review: read Sheet records, Doc tables, comments, and suggestions (gogoogle CLI or mcp-google tools) → assistant writes ReviewResponse → impact-model import review → human runs impact-model patch on accepted proposals files published with links; rows read per origin; stale-hash warnings; rows needing human decision

Manual fallback for toc-share-google: upload the DOCX and CSV by hand, ask reviewers to use the response columns, download the sheet as CSV, and convert it to a ReviewResponse with impact-model import review --from-csv.

Skills that change the theory (impact-author) MUST use impact-model patch or element commands, never write the file directly.

docs.title: 6.12 Editing contract (pkg/edit)
docs.text:
type Patch []Op // RFC 6902: add, remove, replace, move, copy, test
type Result struct {
    Document         *impact.Document
    IssuesIntroduced []validate.Issue
    IssuesResolved   []validate.Issue
    Applied          bool
}
func Apply(doc *impact.Document, p Patch, opts Options) (*Result, error) // opts.AllowErrors
  • Addressing. Standard JSON Pointers plus an ID segment: @<id> selects the element with that id in the array, e.g. /outcomes/@oc-adoption/title or /links/@ln-3. ID segments are resolved to indexes before applying; an unknown ID fails the whole patch.
  • Atomicity. Operations apply to a deep copy (INV-2). If any operation fails, or the result fails schema validation, or error-severity issues increase versus the input (unless AllowErrors), Applied is false and the original is untouched.
  • Element commands build patches: add appends (/outcomes/-) after checking ID uniqueness; set emits replace/add per flag; rm emits remove and, with --cascade, removes or rewrites references (links touching a removed outcome; IDs in appliesTo, assumptionIds, etc.). Without --cascade, dangling references make the patch rejected (INV-4).
  • Writing. The CLI writes the result in canonical form (impact-model fmt), in the input's format. YAML comments are not preserved (PRD R-3).
  • Canonical form. JSON: two-space indent, struct field order, no HTML escaping, trailing newline. YAML: generated from canonical JSON. Element order is preserved; --sort orders elements by ID.

docs.title: 6.13 Presentations (pkg/slides)
docs.text:
Decks are Marp Markdown with a front-matter theme (default, overridable by --theme file.css) and one idea per slide.

Deck Slides workshop Title · problem statement and causes · long-term goal and ceiling of accountability · pathway diagram (whole, then per pathway) · logic model per pathway · key assumptions (if / then / because) · metric definitions · glossary · open questions and decisions exec Headline status · pathway diagram with health · top risks and broken assumptions · what changed since last period · decisions requested · confidence and method footnote learning-review Period summary · surprises · assumption changes · theme counts and selected stories (consented) · questions for discussion · actions story Audience need · three to five headline metrics with caveats · one or two consented stories · call to action

Diagrams: the library embeds Mermaid source in fenced blocks and, when the CLI is asked to export, cmd/impact-model renders each to SVG with mmdc and rewrites the slide to reference the SVG; then runs marp --pdf|--pptx|--html. Missing tools produce exit code 3 with install guidance; the Markdown deck is still written. Same layout conventions as prism-maturity's Marp generator.

docs.title: 6.14 Judging (pkg/judge)
docs.text:
• Bundle (impact-model judge show): JSON with rubric (core or development RubricSet), document (canonical ToC JSON), narrative (generated narrative report Markdown), lint (SummaryReport), instructions (judge instructions from spec/), and bundleHash (SHA-256 of the inputs). The judge (an agent session, visionspec, or visionstudio) reads the bundle; this module makes no model calls.
  • Verdict (impact-model judge record): a structured-evaluation evaluation report whose bundleHash matches; stored as <toc-dir>/.toc/judgements/<bundleHash>/<judge>.json. Mismatched hashes are rejected (the verdict was for a different version).
  • Summary (impact-model judge summary): per category, verdict distribution and inter-rater agreement using structured-evaluation's multi-judge and IRR helpers; overall pass requires the rubric's pass criteria under the configured aggregation (default: majority, ties → partial).

docs.title: 6.15 Sharing, review, and approval (pkg/share, pkg/review)
docs.text:
Export stamp. Every export includes {modelId, version, contentHash, asOf}, where contentHash = SHA-256 of canonical JSON (§6.12). Where it goes:

Format Location Markdown YAML metadata block DOCX / PPTX Inherited from the metadata block, plus a footer line CSV A leading comment row # model:<id> version:<v> hash:<h> Decks Title slide

pandoc profile.

  • Mermaid diagrams are rendered to PNG by mmdc (CLI only) and referenced by relative path.
  • Pipe tables only, with no nested lists inside cells.
  • \newpage markers between sections.
  • The basis badge is rendered as text: [stated], [inferred], [hypothesis].
  • impact-model export docx|pptx runs pandoc -f markdown -t docx|pptx [--reference-doc] with an argument vector (no shell).

Review packet and sheet.

  • Packet layout: one section per element kind (outcomes, links / assumptions, interventions, indicators, metrics, actors). Each section has one table with columns ID | Statement | Basis | Sources | Decision | Suggested change | Comment, with the last three empty.
  • Instructions: the packet asks reviewers to answer in the response columns. Comments and suggestions are still accepted and are mapped by quoted text.
  • Sheet: the same rows, one row per element, with a kind column.

ReviewResponse (schema review-response):

type ReviewResponse struct {
    Kind        string      `json:"kind"`        // "ReviewResponse"
    ModelID       string      `json:"modelId"`
    Version     string      `json:"version"`
    ContentHash string      `json:"contentHash"`
    Reviewers   []string    `json:"reviewers"`   // groups or roles, e.g. "program staff"
    Method      string      `json:"method"`      // document_review | sheet_review | workshop
    Date        string      `json:"date"`
    Rows        []ReviewRow `json:"rows"`
}
type ReviewRow struct {
    ElementID       string `json:"elementId,omitempty"` // empty when only quoted text is known
    Decision        string `json:"decision,omitempty"`  // agree | change | remove | unsure
    SuggestedChange string `json:"suggestedChange,omitempty"`
    Comment         string `json:"comment,omitempty"`
    Origin          string `json:"origin"`              // sheet | table | comment | suggestion
    QuotedText      string `json:"quotedText,omitempty"`
}

Import mapping (impact-model import review):

Row Proposed op agree replace /…/@id/provenance/basis → confirmed remove basis → rejected change with a structured SuggestedChange (field: value lines for title, statement, level, definition, …) replace ops change with free text, unsure, or comment-only Flagged note for a human, not an op No element ID but QuotedText Resolved by exact match against rendered statements. If ambiguous or not found, flagged Stale hash (response hash ≠ document hash) Every row flagged; ops still proposed against current IDs

The import also writes a Consultation record (step whole unless given; method; reviewer groups; findings = row counts by decision).

Approval. impact-model approve builds a patch that sets:

  • metadata.status = approved
  • metadata.version
  • appended Revision{trigger: review, summary, approvers} (prism-core Approver)

It applies the patch through pkg/edit. It refuses when:

  • lint reports any error finding;
  • any rule IMP-PRV-003 violation remains, unless --force with --reason (recorded in the revision).

docs.title: 7.1 Document model (pkg/impact)
docs.text:
Go structs are normative; this table summarizes them. All slices are optional unless marked required.

type Document struct {
    Schema          string           `json:"$schema,omitempty"`
    Kind            string           `json:"kind"`        // "ImpactModel"
    SpecVersion     string           `json:"specVersion"` // "0.1"
    ID              string           `json:"id"`          // doc slug
    Metadata        core.Metadata    `json:"metadata"`    // prism-core
    Perspective     *Perspective     `json:"perspective,omitempty"`
    Context         Context          `json:"context"`
    Ceiling         *Ceiling         `json:"ceilingOfAccountability,omitempty"`
    Outcomes        []Outcome        `json:"outcomes"`
    Groups          []PreconditionGroup `json:"preconditionGroups,omitempty"`
    Links           []CausalLink     `json:"links,omitempty"`

Mission, vision, and values frame the model and are not outcomes; the V2MOM export needs the vision and at least one value. Outcome id, title (req; a positive condition, not an activity), description, level (req: impact, long_term, medium_term, short_term, output), sphere (control, influence, interest), logic {type: all/any/at_least, k} over ungrouped incoming links (default all), category (open string; recommended vocabularies: ORS impact/influence/leverage/capacity, COM-B reach/capability/opportunity/motivation/behavior/direct_benefit/wellbeing, MSD AAER adopt/adapt/expand/respond), changeType (knowledge, attitude, skill, behavior, practice, policy, norm, condition, investment, adoption), population, actorIds[] (who changes / co-owners — supports collective outcomes), contributesTo[] (outcomes in a parent theory, as model:<doc>#<outcome> references; resolved by validate --parent / validate.Family), responsibility (own default, shared, partner, unaddressed), deliveredBy[] (actor IDs), addressesCauses[] (cause IDs), addressesEffects[] (effect IDs), targetGroupIds[], priority? {scores[] {criterionId, score 1–5, note}, rationale}, tags[] Graph node. Indicators reference outcomes, not vice versa. partner / unaddressed outcomes stay in the graph and are monitored (UNDG: monitor the whole solution tree) but are excluded from accountability counts. Problem tree roots; outcomes map to causes via addressesCauses. Causes form a network; validation rejects a cause among its own parents (VAL-CAU-003) and a parent chain that loops (VAL-CAU-004). Effect id, statement (req), parents[] (effect IDs it follows from; empty for a direct effect of the core problem), affectedGroupIds[], evidenceIds[], outOfScope? {reason}, provenance? Problem tree branches; outcomes map to effects via addressesEffects. Validation: a statement (VAL-EFF-001), no effect among its own parents (VAL-EFF-002), no looping parent chain (VAL-EFF-003), a reason when set aside (VAL-EFF-004). PreconditionGroup id, target (outcome ID), members[] (outcome or group IDs; ≥ 2), logic {all/any/at_least, k}, sufficiency (text) Explicit AND/OR/k-of-n "cluster" (ActKnowledge). Groups nest, so (A AND B) OR C is expressible. Incoming links whose source is a group member are evaluated through the group; the group's result feeds the target's logic. Framework-design extensions: metricId (instantiates a shared Metric), pathwayIds[], claim (attribution or contribution; contribution when omitted, so a report never overclaims), caveats[], collection {mode, system, minutesPerPeriod, period, questionsPerRespondent, respondentsPerYear, sampleRate}, selection {status: candidate/selected/retired, scores[] {criterionId, score 1–5, note}, rationale}, audienceIds[], rollupFrom[] (indicator IDs whose values roll up into this one via the metric's rule), themeIds[] (for theme_count indicators derived from stories). measurementType gains theme_count together with the story codebook (RMI-035). Pathway id, title (req), kind (program, strategy, theme, geography, segment), description, ownerActorId, outcomeIds[], interventionIds[], childModel? (ref to a program-level ToC document), focus?, projections[] (dmaic; unique, VAL-PTH-007) Program area / strategy grouping. projections: [dmaic] subjects the pathway's indicators to the IMP-DMA rules and includes it in export dmaic. Indicators join via pathwayIds. A pathway may delegate detail to a child ToC whose parent points back. Metric id, name (req), definition (req), formula (req; exact computation in words, e.g. "sum over sessions of attendees × session hours"), unit, direction, aggregation (sum, mean, weighted_mean, median, mode, min, max, latest, none; median and mode are the honest choices for ordinal levels), weightMetricId?, layer (common, pathway) Shared definition so a metric is computed identically across pathways. none means values cannot be combined (e.g. distinct counts across overlapping populations) and org-level values must be observed directly. SelectionCriterion id, name, question, weight, appliesTo (req: indicator, outcome, intervention) Indicator criteria: decision value, audience value, cost to collect (inverted), consistency, credibility. Outcome / intervention (focus and solution) criteria: equity, comparative advantage, feasibility, evidence of what works. Scores live on the subject (selection.scores for indicators, priority.scores for outcomes and interventions). MeasurementBudget staffMinutesPerWeek, maxQuestionsPerRespondentPerYear, targetSelectedMetrics {min, max} Declared sustainability constraints. Audience id, name (req), needs (what they need to see), channels[] (e.g. annual report, grant proposal, board deck, newsletter) Story and reporting target. GlossaryTerm id (req, so terms can be addressed and referenced), term (req), definition (req), examples[], relatedIds[] Shared vocabulary (e.g. output vs outcome vs impact with organization-specific examples). Theme id, label (req), definition (req), includes[], excludes[], examples[], outcomeIds[] Codebook for coding stories consistently (human or AI). Provenance (embedded as provenance on every element type) basis (stated, inferred, hypothesis, confirmed, rejected), evidenceIds[], note, decidedAt?, decidedBy? (group or role) Public-source drafting and review lifecycle. rejected elements stay in the document for history but are excluded from graph analysis, measurement, and default reports. Sources are ordinary Evidence records (URL, title, excerpt, accessedAt, sensitivity). Indicator dataAvailability public, internal_existing, internal_new, partner_held, unknown Feeds the assessment report and passive-data-first selection. Actor id, name (req), type (organization, person, group, community, customer_segment, government, standards_body, regulator, vendor, platform, investor, other), roles[] (implementer, beneficiary, boundary_partner, funder, champion, influencer, competitor, adopter, gatekeeper), stance (champion, supporter, neutral, skeptic, opponent, unknown), influence/interest (low/medium/high), contact (core.Person), externalRefs[] Shared registry supported via ActorRegistry document. Contradicting evidence lowers link confidence (§6.5). docs.title: 7.2 Observation set and status
docs.text:
type ObservationSet struct {

    IndicatorID string     `json:"indicatorId"`

impact.Status (kind ImpactModelStatus) holds asOf, options (weights / tolerance used), and per-element results: indicators[] (progress, expected, status, health, latest observation), outcomes[] (status, pathwayStatus, confidence, assumptionBroken[]), links[] (state, confidence), assumptions[] (effective status, source), overall (per impact outcome). Field-level schema is generated; this TRD fixes the semantics above.

docs.title: 7.3 USM / UFM integration contract
docs.text:
• Identity: every ToC and element is addressable by §6.7 references.
  • Perspective: Perspective.actorId identifies the market participant (USM) and Perspective.futureRef (ufm:<future-slug>) groups ToCs by competing future (UFM).
  • Shared actors: ActorRegistry documents (kind: ActorRegistry, a list of Actor) let several ToCs reference the same actors; actor IDs from a registry are resolved before INV-1/INV-4 checks.
  • Alignments: BSC objectives and measures attach via Alignment with framework bsc; USM computes its scorecard from ToC Status plus its own BSC data — the ToC never stores BSC data.
  • No back-references: a ToC never lists the USM/UFM models that consume it.

docs.title: 7.4 Data Storage
docs.text: Data Type Storage Rationale ToC documents, observation sets, actor registries Files in git (JSON or YAML) Reviewable diffs, history, PR workflow; no DB in scope Status snapshots Files (JSON), optional commit per period Enables Diff across periods Schemas, template, rubric Embedded in binary and committed Offline use; single source

docs.title: 8. Operational Guarantees
docs.text: Category Requirement Measurement Applicability Performance Validate + lint + status + exec report for 200 outcomes / 400 links / 300 indicators / 5,000 observations in < 1 s on a laptop (Apple M-series) go test -bench benchmarks Applicable Throughput Not applicable — single-user CLI/library — — Availability Not applicable — no service — — Reliability Deterministic outputs (INV-3) Golden tests run twice Applicable Capacity limits PathsToImpact bounded by max (default 1,000) Unit test Applicable Degraded behavior Missing observations yield no_data/stale, never errors Unit tests Applicable Observability Library returns errors; CLI logs via slog to stderr with --verbose Manual Applicable Auditability Every reported status cites inputs (INV-5); git history is the audit trail Report tests Applicable

docs.title: 9. Security and Privacy
docs.text:
• [x] Authentication mechanism — Not applicable: local CLI and stdio MCP; the MCP client process owns authentication.
  • [x] Authorization model — MCP path inputs confined to --root (§6.3).
  • [x] Data encryption at rest — Not applicable: files under the user's control; no storage layer.
  • [x] Data encryption in transit — Not applicable: no network I/O (INV-7).
  • [x] Audit logging — git history plus revision log.
  • [x] Vulnerability scanning — CodeQL (go-sast) and govulncheck in CI; dependencies pinned in go.sum.

Threat model highlights: (1) untrusted documents — parser limits (max file size 10 MB, max 10,000 elements) prevent memory exhaustion; (2) user report templates run text/template with no custom functions that touch the filesystem or network; (3) restricted evidence never rendered (INV-6); (4) MCP path traversal blocked; (5) personal data — the model is designed for aggregate observations; stories identify actors by registry ID (which may be an anonymized label), quotes require consent: granted, and documentation directs users to keep personal records (contacts, sign-ups) in their source systems and import only aggregates; (6) theme coding provenance is recorded (codedBy) so model-coded stories can be audited; (7) external export tools are invoked with fixed binary names and argument vectors (no shell), on files the CLI itself wrote; (8) agent edits are confined to validated patches (INV-9), so a misbehaving agent cannot leave a document invalid without --allow-errors.

docs.title: 10. Compatibility and Migration Guarantees
docs.text:
Applicability: Applicable from the first tagged release.

  • Supported versions: specVersion 0.1; loaders reject unknown majors.
  • Forward / backward compatibility: v0.x minors are additive; unknown fields are rejected by schema (additionalProperties: false) to catch typos, so a newer document fails on an older binary with a clear error.
  • Mixed-version deployment: Not applicable — no service.
  • Migration phases: major bumps ship impact-model migrate converting the previous major.
  • Data validation: migrated documents must pass impact-model validate.
  • Rollback boundary: documents are files in git; rollback is a revert.

docs.title: 11. Dependencies
docs.text:
Dependency Version (verified) Purpose Criticality Go 1.26+ Language (org standard) High github.com/grokify/prism-core v0.5.0 Metadata, Person, Risk, health, trend, CapabilityRef High github.com/grokify/prism-roadmap v0.21.0 OKR / OutcomeJourney export (adapter only) Medium github.com/plexusone/structured-evaluation v0.14.0 summary.SummaryReport, rubric.RubricSet High github.com/invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 Schema generation High github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3 (same as prism-maturity) Schema validation High sigs.k8s.io/yaml latest verified at implementation time YAML → JSON Medium github.com/spf13/cobra v1.10.2 CLI Medium github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk latest verified at implementation time (≥ v1.8.0) MCP server Medium schemakit (tool) installed Schema lint in CI Medium @marp-team/marp-cli (optional external) latest at use Deck export to PDF / PPTX / HTML Low — Markdown deck works without it @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc (optional external) latest at use Diagram → SVG for decks, PNG for the pandoc profile Low — Mermaid source works without it pandoc (optional external) 3.x at use Markdown → DOCX / PPTX for sharing Low — Markdown export works without it Google Drive tooling (external, used only by the toc-share-google skill) gogoogle CLI with driveutil (from INIT-GOGOOGLE-001) and mcp-google comments/suggestions tools (from INIT-MCPGOOGLE-001) Upload with conversion; read comments, suggestions, Sheets Low — manual upload and CSV review sheet are the fallback

docs.title: 12. Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Unit tests per package, table-driven; t.Fatal on errors.
  • Golden files in testdata/ for lint reports, status snapshots, and reports; -update flag regenerates.
  • Seeded-defect corpus: one fixture per lint rule.
  • Property tests: random DAGs for graph invariants (paths end at impact, levels monotone).
  • Import-boundary test (TRD-014).
  • Schema drift test (TRD-003) and embedded-schema load test.
  • MCP in-memory transport test (TRD-013).
  • Benchmarks for §8 performance.
  • Coverage ≥ 80 % on pkg/....

docs.title: 13.1 Rollout and Feature Flags
docs.text: Not applicable — library and CLI released as tagged Go module versions (go install …/cmd/impact-model@vX.Y.Z). Releases follow the org release process (CHANGELOG.json via structured-changelog; tag after CI is green).

docs.title: 13.2 Rollback Plan
docs.text: Consumers pin module versions; rollback is pinning the previous tag. Published tags are immutable, so fixes roll forward.

docs.title: 14. Alternatives Considered
docs.text: Alternative Why rejected Hand-written JSON Schema as the source of truth Violates org Go-first policy; drifts from code Embed observations inside the ToC document Couples slow-changing theory with per-period data; noisy diffs; harder agent edits. Rejected for separate ObservationSet Model the ToC as a logframe (fixed input → activity → output → outcome → impact rows) Cannot express multiple pathways, AND/OR preconditions, or feedback; loses the ToC's main value Adjacency stored on outcomes (preconditions: [ids]) instead of first-class links Links need their own rationale, assumptions, evidence, and confidence; first-class edges keep those addressable Reuse prism-roadmap common.Assumption Lacks type, criticality, appliesTo, test, and status needed for propagation; ToC-specific type is justified, and prism-core has no assumption type Wrap structured-evaluation claims.Claim for evidence (as prism-roadmap assessment does) Heavier than needed for v0; revisit when evidence verification by LLM judges is in scope Graph database or Dolt storage Out of scope; git files suffice for document-sized graphs Per-outcome logic only (no groups) Cannot express nested logic such as (A AND B) OR C; ActKnowledge "clusters" and Davies' critique both call for explicit joint preconditions Interventions only as nodes with outgoing links (logic-model style) ActKnowledge places interventions on connectors ("what it takes for A to produce B"); both placements are supported via Intervention.targets and CausalLink.interventionIds Agents rewrite whole documents (no patch engine) Large, unreviewable diffs; easy to drop elements silently; no atomic validation. Patches are small, reviewable, and checkable before write Third-party JSON Patch library (e.g. evanphx/json-patch) Lacks ID-segment addressing and error-delta rejection; wrapping it still needs a custom resolver; the in-house engine over impact.Model JSON is small and fully tested Generate PPTX directly from Go Large dependency and layout effort; Marp gives Markdown-native decks consistent with prism-maturity, with PDF/PPTX export as an optional step Import Google Drive SDK into this module to publish and read reviews Couples a spec library to one cloud; violates INV-7; the file-based ReviewResponse lets any channel (Google, Microsoft 365, email, workshop notes) feed the same import Apply review responses directly Free-text feedback needs judgment; proposals plus impact-model patch keep a human decision on every change and keep INV-9 Marp PPTX for shared decks Marp's PPTX is image-based, so Google Slides conversion yields non-editable, unreadable slides; Pandoc PPTX keeps native text Judge inside this module via an LLM SDK Violates the no-LLM-dependency non-goal; bundle + verdict files let any judge (agent, visionspec, visionstudio) participate and keep results auditable Closed enum for outcome category Development (ORS, COM-B), market-systems (AAER), and corporate ToCs need different taxonomies; category is an open string with documented recommended vocabularies

docs.title: 14.1 Deferred extensions (reserved names)
docs.text: From the research brief §8.4, these are deferred to a later initiative and their names are reserved so v0 documents do not collide: contributionClaims (Contribution Analysis), observedOutcomes (Outcome Harvesting with substantiation; an unmapped observed outcome becomes a revision prompt — Most-Significant-Change-style stories are in scope via ObservationSet.stories), and logframe matrix projections (per-pathway logic-model views are in scope). The UNDG problem tree is in scope as Model.causes (research §9.8).

docs.title: 15. Risks and Open Questions
docs.text:
ID Risk / Question Impact Mitigation / Resolution Q-1 Should output be an outcome level or a separate type? Model shape Resolved: outcome level output, so outputs can be measured and linked uniformly; interventions also list free-text outputs Q-2 Default roll-up worst may look pessimistic to executives Adoption Configurable; exec report states the method Q-3 Confidence weights are opinionated Trust Defaults documented, overridable, printed with every score R-1 schemakit may flag map[string]string disaggregation Lint failure Replace with []KeyValue if flagged R-2 prism-core Metadata uses omitzero time fields; schema generation of time.Time Schema shape Accept date-time format; covered by schema tests

No open question blocks implementation.
